Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 14, verses 1–3:

This surah is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1–2} He, exalted is He, informs that He sent down His Book to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) for the benefit of creation, so that He might bring people out of the darknesses of ignorance, disbelief, bad character and various kinds of sin into the light of knowledge, faith and good character. His saying {by the permission of their Lord} means that the desired goal beloved to Allah is not attained by them except by will from Allah and His help; in this is an exhortation to the servants to seek help from their Lord. Then He explained the light to which this Book guides them, saying {to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy}; that is, the path that leads to Him and to the abode of His honour, which encompasses knowledge of the truth and acting upon it. Mentioning "the Mighty, the Praiseworthy" after mentioning the path that leads to Him is an indication that whoever travels it is mighty through the might of Allah, strong even if he has no helpers but Allah, praiseworthy in his affairs, and good in his final outcome. It also shows that the path of Allah is among the greatest proofs of the attributes of perfection and the exalted qualities that belong to Allah, and that He who established it for His servants is mighty in authority and praiseworthy in His words, deeds and judgments, and that He is the One worthy of worship, served through the acts of worship which are the stations of the straight path. And just as He has dominion over the heavens and the earth in creation, provision and management, so He has the right to judge His servants by His religious rulings, because they are His possession, and it is not fitting for Him to leave them neglected. When He had clarified the proof and evidence, He threatened those who do not submit to that, saying {And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment}: its extent cannot be estimated and its matter cannot be described.

{3} Then He described them as those who prefer {the worldly life over the Hereafter}: they are content with it, settle in it, and become heedless of the Hereafter. {And who averse [others] from} {the way of Allah}: the way which He established for His servants, clarified in His Books and upon the tongues of His Messengers; such people have openly defied their Master with enmity and warfare. {And seek to make it crooked}; that is, the way of Allah: they strive to disfigure and defame it in order to repel people from it. But Allah refuses except to perfect His light, even if the disbelievers dislike it. {Those} whose description has been mentioned {are in far-reaching error}: because they have gone astray and led others astray, opposed Allah and His Messenger and waged war against them; so what error is further than this? As for the people of faith, they are the opposite of these: they believe in Allah and His signs, they prefer the Hereafter over the world, they call to the way of Allah, they beautify it as much as they can, and they make its uprightness clear.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 14, verses 9–12:

{9} God, the Exalted, says, warning His servants of what He inflicted upon the nations that denied, when their messengers came to them and they denied them, so He punished them with the swift punishment that people saw and heard. He says: ﴿Has there not come to you the news of those before you: the people of Noah, and 'Ad, and Thamud﴾. God has mentioned their stories in His Book and elaborated upon them. ﴿And those after them, none knows them but God﴾: because of their multitude and because their reports have been effaced. All of these ﴿came to them with their messengers, with clear proofs﴾; that is, with evidences indicating the truth of what they brought. God did not send any messenger except that He gave him signs by which humankind would believe in the like of them. So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they did not submit to them, but rather were arrogant towards them, ﴿and they put their hands to their mouths﴾; that is, they did not believe in what they had brought, and did not utter anything that indicates faith, like His saying: ﴿they put their fingers in their ears because of the thunderbolts, fearing death﴾. ﴿And they said﴾ plainly to their messengers: ﴿Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and indeed we are, concerning that to which you invite us, in disquieting doubt﴾; that is, in doubt that causes unease.

{10} They lied in this and did wrong, and therefore ﴿their messengers said﴾ to them: ﴿Is there doubt about God?﴾; that is, for He is the most manifest and evident of things. Whoever doubts God, ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, upon whose existence the existence of things depends, will have no certainty about any of the known things, even sensible matters. Therefore the messengers addressed them as one who is not in doubt about Him, and for whom doubt is not fitting. ﴿He calls you﴾ to your benefits and your welfare, ﴿that He may forgive you of your sins and delay you until a specified term﴾; that is, that He may reward you for responding to His call with reward both in this world and in the next. He did not call you so that He would benefit from your worship; rather, the benefit returns to you. So they answered their messengers with the response of foolish ignorant people, ﴿and they said﴾ to them: ﴿You are not but human beings like us﴾; that is, how then do you surpass us in prophethood and messengership? ﴿You want to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship﴾: how then shall we abandon the opinion and conduct of our fathers for your opinion? And how shall we obey you when you are human beings like us? ﴿So bring us a clear authority﴾; that is, a proof and a manifest evidence. Their intent is a sign that they themselves propose; otherwise, it has already been stated that their messengers had come to them with clear proofs.

{11} ﴿Their messengers said to them﴾, responding to their proposal and objection: ﴿We are only human beings like you﴾; that is, it is true and a fact that we are human beings like you. ﴿But﴾ this does not repel the truth we have brought, for ﴿God bestows favor upon whom He wills of His servants﴾. So if God has favored us with His revelation and His messengership, that is His grace and kindness, and no one may restrict God's grace or prevent Him from bestowing it. Consider what we have brought you: if it is true, accept it, and if it is otherwise, reject it, and do not make our condition a pretext for you to reject what we have brought you. As for your saying ﴿So bring us a clear authority﴾, this is not in our hands, and we have no say in the matter. ﴿It was not for us to bring you an authority except by God's permission﴾: He is the One who, if He wills, brings it to you, and if He wills, does not bring it to you, and He does nothing except what is required by His wisdom and mercy. ﴿And upon God﴾, not upon anyone else, ﴿let the believers rely﴾: relying on Him to bring about their benefits and repel their harms, knowing His complete sufficiency, perfect power and abundant kindness, and trusting Him to facilitate that; and their reliance is in proportion to the faith they have. From this it is known that reliance (tawakkul) is obligatory, that it is one of the requirements of faith and among the great acts of worship that God loves and is pleased with, since all other acts of worship depend upon it.

{12} ﴿And why should we not rely upon God, when He has guided us to our ways?﴾; that is, what prevents us from relying upon God when we are upon the truth and guidance? Whoever is upon the truth and guidance, his guidance necessitates for him complete reliance, and likewise what is known of God's undertaking to aid and suffice the one who is guided calls to that; unlike one who is not upon the truth and guidance, for he has no guarantee from God, since his condition contradicts the condition of one who relies? And in this there is, as it were, an indication from the messengers, peace be upon them, to their people of a great sign, namely that their people generally have power and dominance over them. So their messengers challenged them, saying that they rely upon God to repel their plots and schemes, and are certain of His sufficiency for them, and God has indeed sufficed them against their evil despite their eagerness to destroy them and extinguish the truth they possessed. This is like the saying of Noah to his people: ﴿O my people, if my standing and my reminding you of the signs of God is burdensome to you, then upon God I rely. So resolve your affair with your partners, then let not your affair be obscured to you; then carry it out upon me and do not give me respite…﴾ and the verses that follow, and the saying of Hud, peace be upon him: ﴿He said, "Indeed, I call God to witness, and bear witness, you, that I am free from what you associate besides Him. So scheme against me all together, then give me no respite."﴾ ﴿And we will surely be patient over what you have inflicted upon us﴾: we will persist in our call, admonition and reminding you, and not mind the harm that comes to us from you; for we shall accustom ourselves to what harm reaches us from you, seeking reward and giving counsel to you, perhaps God will guide you despite the abundance of reminding. ﴿And upon God﴾ alone, not upon anyone else, ﴿let those who rely upon Him rely﴾, for reliance upon Him is the key to every good.

Know that the reliance of the messengers, peace be upon them, was at the highest of aims and the most noble of ranks, namely reliance upon God in establishing His religion, supporting it, guiding His servants, and removing misguidance from them. This is the most perfect form of reliance.

This is among the greatest injustices, for Allah brought His servants out onto the earth, commanded them to worship Him, and subjected the earth and what is upon it to them, so that they might use it to worship Him. Whoever uses that to worship Allah, it becomes lawful for him and he is free of accountability; and whoever uses it for disbelief and various kinds of sin, it is not purely his and is not lawful for him. Thus it is known that the enemies of the messengers, in reality, have no share in the land with which they threatened the messengers to expel them from it. And if we return merely to custom: the messengers are among the people of their lands and are individuals from among them; so for what reason would they prevent them from a right that is clear and manifest? Is this anything other than a complete lack of religion and chivalry? For this reason, when their scheming against the messengers reached this state, nothing remained except that Allah carry out His command and grant victory to His allies. {So their Lord revealed to them: We will surely destroy the wrongdoers}: with various kinds of punishment.

{14} {And We will surely settle you in the land after them}; that is, the good outcome which Allah made a reward for the messengers and those who followed them, {for whoever fears My standing (before Me)}: in this world, and who watches over (his conduct before) Allah as one who knows that He sees him, {and fears My threat}; that is, what I have threatened against whoever disobeys Me; so this obliges him to refrain from what Allah dislikes and to hasten to what Allah loves.

{16} {Behind him is Hell}; that is, Hell lies in wait for this obstinate tyrant; so he will inevitably arrive at it, and then he will taste the severe punishment. {And he will be given to drink of putrid water}: foul in its color, taste, and odor, and it is at the extreme of heat.

{17} {He will gulp it down}: from intense thirst, {yet he will scarcely be able to swallow it}: for when it is brought near his face, it scorches it, and when it reaches his belly, it cuts through whatever it passes over of his intestines. {Death will come to him from every place, yet he will not die}; that is, severe punishment will come to him from every kind of punishment, and each kind of it, from its severity, reaches to death, but Allah decreed that they should not die, as He said, Exalted is He: {It will not be decreed for them to die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them. Verse 18: God informs us about the deeds of the disbelievers that they performed. It may be that what is meant is the deeds they did for God's sake, which will come to nothing, vanish and disintegrate, like the ashes that are the finest and lightest of things when a strong wind blows on a violently stormy day. It leaves nothing of them, and no one is able to gather any of them back. Likewise are the deeds of the disbelievers: ﴿They have no power over anything of what they have earned﴾, not even the weight of an atom's particle, because it is built upon disbelief and denial. ﴿That is the far-reaching error﴾: in that their striving has been lost and their deeds have come to nothing. Or it may be that what is meant by this is the deeds of the disbelievers that they performed in order to scheme against the truth. They strive and toil in that, but their scheming rebounds upon them, and they will never harm God, His messengers, His soldiers, or what they possess of the truth in any way.

{19} Almighty God reminds His servants that He {created the heavens and the earth in truth}; that is, so that creation would worship Him, know Him, and so that He would command them and forbid them; and so that they would reflect upon these two and what is in them as evidence of His attributes of perfection; and so that they would know that He who created the heavens and the earth, despite their greatness and vastness, is able to bring them back as a new creation, so that He may recompense them for their good and their evil, and that His power and will do not fall short of that.
For this reason He said: {If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation}. It may be understood that the meaning is: if He wills, He can take you away and bring other people who will be more obedient to God than you. It may also be that the intended meaning is: if He wills, He can annihilate you and then restore you by resurrection as a new creation. This second interpretation is supported by what He mentions after it concerning the conditions of the Resurrection.

{24} God, exalted is He, says: {Have you not considered how God presents a parable: a good word}, which is the testimony that there is no god but God (la ilaha illa Allah) and its branches, {like a good tree}, which is the date palm, {whose root is firmly fixed}, in the earth, {and whose branches are in the sky}, meaning that it is always abundantly beneficial.

This is from His mercy and His excellent instruction; so to God belongs the most complete, perfect and all-encompassing praise. This is the description of the word of monotheism and its firmness in the heart of the believer.

{31} That is: say to My believing servants, commanding them with that which contains the utmost of their welfare, and that they seize the opportunity before it becomes impossible for them to do so: {establish the prayer}, outwardly and inwardly, {and spend out of what We have provided for them}; that is, out of the blessings which We have bestowed upon them, whether little or much, {secretly and openly}. This includes obligatory spending such as zakat and the maintenance of those whose maintenance is obligatory upon one, and recommended spending such as voluntary charities and the like. {Before there comes a Day in which there is no trading, nor any friendship}; that is, in which nothing will benefit, and there is no way to make up for what has passed, neither by an exchange of buying and selling, nor by the gift of a close friend or companion. Therefore let the servant send forward for his soul, let him look at what he has sent forward for tomorrow, let him review his deeds, and take account of himself before the Greatest Reckoning.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 14, verse 32–34:

{32} He, may He be exalted, informs that He alone is the One ﴿who created the heavens and the earth﴾, despite their vastness and immensity, ﴿and sent down water from the sky﴾, which is the rain that Allah sends down from the clouds, and by that water He brings forth ﴿fruits of various kinds as provision for you﴾, and provision for your livestock. ﴿And He subjected the ships for you﴾, that is, the boats and vessels, ﴿to sail through the sea by His command﴾. He is the One who facilitated for you their construction, empowered you to use them, and kept them afloat on the current of the water, so that they carry you, your merchandise and your goods to a land you intend. ﴿And He subjected the rivers for you﴾, so that they irrigate your crops and trees, and so that you may drink from them.

{33} ﴿And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, both constantly pursuing their courses﴾, neither tiring nor slackening, striving for your benefit by reckoning your times, and for the welfare of your bodies, your animals, your crops and your fruits. ﴿And He subjected for you the night﴾ that you may rest therein, ﴿and the day, giving light﴾ that you may seek of His bounty.

{34} ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked Him﴾, that is, He gave you of everything your hopes and needs were attached to, of what you ask Him for, whether by the tongue of your state or by the tongue of your speech, such as livestock, tools, crafts and other things. ﴿And if you were to count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾, let alone fulfil its thanks. ﴿Indeed, mankind is excessively unjust and ungrateful﴾, that is, this is the nature of man insofar as he is unjust, bold in disobedience, negligent of the rights of his Lord, and ungrateful for the blessings of Allah, not thanking for them nor acknowledging them, except for those whom Allah guides, so that they give thanks for His blessings, recognize the right of their Lord and fulfil it.

In these verses there is, among the kinds of Allah's blessings upon His servants, a great matter, both in summary and in detail, which calls the servants, through Allah, to fulfil His thanks and remembrance, urges them to do so, and encourages them to ask and supplicate Him at all hours of the night and day; just as His blessing is continually renewed upon them at all times.

{35} Remember Abraham (peace be upon him) in this beautiful state, when Abraham said: "My Lord, make this city (i.e., the Sacred Precinct, al-Haram) secure." God answered his supplication both legislatively and by decree: He made it sacred in the Law, and by decree He facilitated, through causes known to Him, its sanctity, to the extent that no oppressor intended it with evil except that God crushed him, as He did with the People of the Elephant and others. And when he asked for security for it, he also asked for security for himself and his sons, saying: "And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols"; that is, make me and them far removed from worshipping them and from coming near them.

{36} Then he mentioned the reason for his fear for himself and his sons: the great number of those who were seduced and tested by worshipping them. He said: "My Lord, they have indeed led many people astray." That is, they caused them to go astray. "Whoever follows me" in what I have brought of monotheism and sincere devotion to God, Lord of the worlds, "then he is of me," due to complete agreement; and whoever loves a people and follows them is joined with them. "And whoever disobeys me, then You are Forgiving and Merciful." This is from the compassion of the Friend (Khalil) (peace be upon him), in that he asked for forgiveness and mercy from God for the disobedient; and God, blessed and exalted, is more merciful to His servants than he is, and He does not punish except those who rebel against Him.

{37} "Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House." That is because he brought Hajar, the mother of Isma'il, and her son Isma'il (peace be upon him), while he was still nursing, from al-Sham until he placed them in Makkah, and at that time there was no dwelling there, no caller, and no answerer. When he left them, he supplicated his Lord with this supplication, saying, humbly and reliant upon his Lord: "Lord, I have settled some of my offspring"; that is, not all my offspring, because Isḥaq was in al-Sham and his remaining sons were likewise; rather, he settled in Makkah Isma'il and his descendants. His words "in an uncultivated valley" mean that the land of Makkah is not suitable for agriculture. "Our Lord, that they may establish prayer" means: make them monotheists who establish prayer, because establishing prayer is among the most distinguished and excellent religious acts; whoever establishes it has established his religion. "So make hearts among the people incline toward them" means: that they love them and love the place in which they dwell. God answered his supplication, and from the descendants of Isma'il He brought forth Muhammad (ﷺ), until he called his descendants to the religion of Islam and to the creed of their father Abraham, and they responded to him and became establishers of prayer. God made obligatory the pilgrimage to this House in which He settled his descendants, Abraham, and placed in it a wondrous secret that draws hearts; so hearts make pilgrimage to it and never fulfill their need from it permanently; rather, the more the servant frequents it, the more his longing increases, his love grows great, and his yearning intensifies. This is the secret of its ascription to God's own sacred Self. "And provide them with fruits, that they may be grateful." God answered his supplication, and so there is brought to it the fruits of everything; for you see the honored city of Makkah at all times with abundant fruits, and provisions continually arrive to it from every side.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 14, verses 47–52:**

{47} He, exalted is He, says: {So do not think that Allah would fail to fulfill His promise to His messengers}: [that is, regarding] their salvation, the salvation of their followers and their happiness, and the destruction of their enemies and their humiliation in this world and their punishment in the Hereafter. This must come to pass, because the One who is true in speech has promised it through the tongues of the most truthful of His creation, who are the messengers, and this is the highest kind of report, especially since it accords with divine wisdom, the divine customs (sunan rabbaniyyah) and sound reason. Allah, exalted is He, is not incapable of anything, for He is {Mighty, Possessor of retribution}; that is, when He wills to take retribution from anyone, He cannot be escaped or thwarted. And that will be on the Day of Resurrection.

{48} {On the Day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens [as well]}: it will be changed, and so will the heavens. This change is a change of attributes, not a change of essence. On the Day of Resurrection the earth will be leveled and stretched out like a hide, and whatever is on its surface of mountains and landmarks will be cast away, so it becomes a smooth, level plain in which you see no crookedness or elevation. The sky will be like molten brass because of the severity of the terrors of that Day. Then Allah, exalted is He, will fold it up in His right hand. {And they will come forth}; that is, the creatures will come forth from their graves until the day of their resurrection and gathering, in a place where nothing of them is hidden from Allah, {before Allah, the One, the Subduer}; that is, the One alone in His greatness, His names, His attributes and His great acts, and in His subjugation of all worlds, so that all of them are under His control and governance. Nothing moves except by His permission, and nothing is still except by His leave.

{49} {And you will see the criminals}; that is, those characterized by criminality and abundance of sins on that Day, {bound together in shackles}; that is, every group of criminals of the same deeds will be chained together with chains of fire, and they will be led to punishment in the most humiliating, ugliest and most hideous form.

{50} {Their garments}; that is, their clothing {of pitch}: this is because of the intensity of the burning of the fire upon them, its heat and the foulness of its smell. {And the Fire will cover their faces}: which are the most noble part of their bodies; that is, it will surround them and burn them from every side. What is other than the faces is all the more so, and more fitting.

{51} This is not injustice from Allah [toward them]; rather it is a recompense for what they have sent forth and earned. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: {That Allah may recompense every soul for what it has earned}: of good and evil, with justice and equity in which there is no oppression in any way. {Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning}; like His saying: {The reckoning has drawn near for the people, while they are in heedlessness, turning away}. It is also possible that the meaning is "swift in calling to account": He reckons with creation in a single hour, just as He provides for them and manages them with various arrangements in a single moment. No affair preoccupies Him from another affair, and that is not difficult for Him.

{52} When He had made clear the clear explanation in this Qur'an, He said in praising it: {This is a message for mankind}; that is, they may take provision from it and equip themselves to reach the highest stations and the best honors, because it includes the fundamentals and the branches and all the sciences that the servants need. {And that they may be warned thereby}: because of what it contains of warning against evil deeds and the punishment Allah has prepared for their doers. {And that they may know that He is but one God}: in that He has set forth in it the proofs and evidences of His divinity and His oneness, to the point that this becomes the certainty of certainties. {And that those of understanding may be reminded}; that is, those of complete intellects [may be reminded] of what benefits them so that they do it, and what harms them so that they abandon it. Through this they become people of understanding and insight, for through the Qur'an their knowledge and opinions increase, and their thoughts are illuminated when they receive it fresh and tender. It calls only to the highest and best of morals and deeds, and it proves that only with the strongest and clearest proofs. When an intelligent servant trains himself by this principle, he will always remain in ascent and elevation in every praiseworthy quality. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

*The tafsir of Surah Ibrahim, upon him be peace, is complete.*
